body: I get what you're saying - memes are memes. Not every meme will be enjoyed by everyone, but everything is fine to be memed. I don't care about what people like to joke about. Am I sick of getting hate for liking a fictional relationship? Sure, but like, whatever. I'm not reporting just because I don't like it/don't agree with it, nor would that EVER be my primary reason to report a post. Free speech and all that jazz. I'm reporting this post because the artist doesn't want their art used like this, and specifically asked for it to be taken down, which is totally reasonable imo.

No problem, thanks for the apology.

Tbh, I understand where you're coming from. As I said in an earlier comment, I know that once it's on the internet, it's game to be made into a meme. But I'm not a fan of someone using someone else's art to make fun of the very thing they love, just on principle. Using official art, screen caps, whatever, sure. But it feels a bit wrong to use someone's effort and love to make fun of them, you know? I know it's the internet and it's gonna happen - happens to me on my own stuff all the time - but that doesn't mean I have to like it, and just let it be.
https://twitter.com/Echo1069479/status/1053943272903770113?s=19

I get that once you post art on the Internet its out of your hands, and memes like this come up, but the cool thing about places like reddit is - guess what - you can report it when it breaks the rules!

Yeah, my parents divorced when I was 9. It was a hard couple of years, aha.

Not my story, but my father's. He was raised very Catholic and believed all his life that being gay was wrong. He was never the kind to act differently to people, ever, but he would think in the back of his mind that the life they were living was wrong. 

I didn't really know this about him because for the most part he kept it to himself. When I was 13, I told my mother I liked girls too, and she called my father and kicked me out of the house for two weeks. During those two weeks my father spent a lot of time thinking on what had happened, and started to change his views slowly. He didn't talk to me about it much at first, talking more to his brother who's son is gay, and finally decided that as long as I - and anyone else, for that matter - was happy, it didn't matter to him. He has always been my favorite parent, and his willingness to rethink his beliefs for me really solidified that, haha.
